Emily — thanks, quick technical notes to make the smoke tests smooth: 

1) Header/API compatibility: Redwood's OpenAI-compatible surface supports Authorization: Bearer <key> and the same JSON payloads (model, messages, prompt, max_tokens, temperature). We also accept the X-Request-ID header for tracing. No X-OpenAI-* headers required.

2) SDK swaps: if you're using the standard openai-js/python clients, you can point the base_url to our endpoint and pass your Redwood key. Example (node):

// snippet start
const OpenAI = require('openai');
const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, baseURL: 'https://api.redwood.com/v1' });
const res = await client.responses.create({ model: 'redwood-compat-1', input: 'Summarize ...' });
// snippet end

For python: set openai.api_base and openai.api_key similarly. We'll include these snippets in the PDF.

3) Prompt diffs: small token delta is expected (different tokenizer and generation seeds). For ranking/similarity/regression checks, we recommend:
- Thresholds: <= 2% mean-generation token delta and <= 3% difference in top-1 label change for classification/rerank tasks.
- For safety/critical outputs: exact-match tests plus a manual review.

4) Perf: we'll provide a short benchmark (p50/p95) using FinCo's sample payload sizes. If you can share a small workload sample (20 representative requests, anonymized), we'll run with identical concurrency.

If you hit any auth 401s, ping me directly. I'll also open a temporary test key and add it to the Drive link in the guide.

—Vivek
